prompt: A session typed on the train has not been sent yet. Which kind of local data is it?

choices.text: Pinned for offline
choices.why: Pinning is the person asking to keep a copy of something the server has.

choices.text: A cache entry, since the server will have it later
choices.why: Later is the problem: tonight, nothing else has it.

choices.text: Source of truth
choices.why: Right. Until the outbox delivers it, the phone holds the only copy.

choices.text: Temporary data that belongs in tmp/
choices.why: tmp/ is emptied by the system, which would lose the session.

prompt: The person pins a course's notes for a flight. The cover-picture cache needs room. What may happen to the notes?

choices.text: Nothing, until the person unpins them
choices.why: Right. A pinned item is kept, and its size is shown to the person.

choices.text: Evicted if they are the least recently used
choices.why: That is the rule for a cache. A pin is a promise to the person.

choices.text: Evicted first, being the largest item
choices.why: Size decides eviction among cache entries; pinned notes are not one.

choices.text: Moved to Library/Caches/ to free the database
choices.why: That would hand them to the system to delete.

prompt: Match each piece of the planner's data to the kind it is.
What does a server's 304 Not Modified tell the planner?

choices.text: The resource was deleted and the copy should go
choices.why: Deletion is a 404 or 410; 304 says the opposite.

choices.text: The request was malformed
choices.why: That is a 400.

choices.text: Try again later
choices.why: That would be a 503 or a 429.

choices.text: It is still current; keep it
choices.why: Right, and the answer carries no body, which is what makes the check cheap.

prompt: With max-age=60 and stale-while-revalidate=300, the copy was downloaded at second 0. What does the planner do at second 90?

choices.text: Shows nothing until the network answers
choices.why: That is after second 360, when the copy is too old to show.

choices.text: Shows the old copy, and checks behind it
choices.why: Right. In the lesson's run that check came back 200 with Chess in it.

choices.text: Deletes the copy and downloads the whole body again
choices.why: An expired copy is checked, not thrown away.

choices.text: Shows the copy and asks the server nothing
choices.why: That is the fresh window, which ended at second 60.

prompt: In the lesson's run, the catalogue changed at second 40 and the screen at second 45 still showed three courses. What does the lesson make of that?

choices.text: A bug in fetch.ts: it should ask at each read
choices.why: Asking on every read is what max-age exists to avoid.

choices.text: The price of max-age, paid knowingly for 60 seconds
choices.why: Right. Freshness means trusting a copy over the network for that long.

choices.text: A broken ETag, because the server did not change it
choices.why: The tag did change; at second 90 it no longer matched.

choices.text: Proof that the session list should be cached for longer
choices.why: The session list is not cached this way at all; lesson 11 pulls it with a cursor.

prompt: To ask whether its copy changed, the client sends the tag it holds in the ___ header.
In the lesson's run of six reads, how many requests reached the server?
Why does the lesson give the cache a budget in bytes rather than in entries?

choices.text: SQLite counts rows slowly once the cache holds thousands of them
choices.why: Speed has nothing to do with it.

choices.text: Entries are harder to evict
choices.why: Eviction works the same; the question is when to start.

choices.text: The platforms' HTTP caches refuse a limit given in entries
choices.why: They refuse nothing; it is the wrong measure.

choices.text: Pictures differ widely in size, and the disk is what runs out
choices.why: Right. A hundred entries can be 4 MB or 400.

prompt: In the run, Spanish was stored first but Statistics was evicted. Why?

choices.text: `get spanish` made Spanish recently used
choices.why: Right. The hit moved it to the back of the queue.

choices.text: The cache evicts in alphabetical order
choices.why: Order is by last use, not by name.

choices.text: Statistics was the largest picture
choices.why: It was 3 MB, smaller than Spanish's 4 MB.

choices.text: Statistics had expired
choices.why: lru.ts has no expiry; it only has a budget.

prompt: Why does lru.ts order its entries with a counter instead of the time of use?

choices.text: A counter takes less space in the table than a full timestamp does
choices.why: Both are integers; space is not the argument.

choices.text: Node cannot read the time inside SQLite
choices.why: It can; that is not why.

choices.text: LRU needs an order, and a corrected clock could move backwards
choices.why: Right. A counter cannot go backwards when the phone's clock is set.

choices.text: Times would make the cache expire its entries on a schedule of their own
choices.why: Ordering by time would not add expiry; the problem is the order itself.

prompt: Put in order what `put` does in lru.ts when a new cover does not fit.
items: finds the least recently used entry
writes the new file and its row

prompt: When may iOS empty an app's Library/Caches/?

choices.text: When the disk is nearly full
choices.why: Right, even with the app closed. That is the agreement the folder's name makes.

choices.text: When the person asks in Settings
choices.why: The system does it on its own when the disk is nearly full.

choices.text: Not at all; Caches is backed up and kept
choices.why: Caches is neither backed up nor kept.

choices.text: At each update of the app, when the container is rebuilt from scratch
choices.why: An update keeps the container.

prompt: After `rm -rf cache.db covers covers.db`, both programs carried on. What in their code made that so?

choices.text: A try/catch around every line
choices.why: Neither has one; they never meet the error.

choices.text: A backup of the cache in the database
choices.why: Backing up a cache would make it a second source of truth.

choices.text: Each creates what it needs, and checks before it reads
choices.why: Right: create table if not exists, mkdir, and existsSync in get.

choices.text: The system restores the folder from the backup on the next launch
choices.why: It restores nothing; the app fetches again.

prompt: A library defaulted to putting the planner's database in Library/Caches/. Testing finds nothing wrong for months. What does the lesson predict?

choices.text: No harm: iOS backs up Caches when it holds a database
choices.why: iOS leaves Caches out whatever it holds.

choices.text: The sessions vanish the day the disk fills
choices.why: Right. The cache is the system's to empty, and it held the only copy.

choices.text: Slower reads, because Caches is on a different disk
choices.why: It is the same disk; the risk is deletion.

choices.text: The database is moved to Documents/ at the next update
choices.why: Nothing moves it.

prompt: Which of these may live under the LRU rule of lru.ts? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: a course's cover picture
choices.why: It can be downloaded again.

choices.text: a thumbnail of a picture the server keeps
choices.why: Also a copy of something the server has.

choices.text: a session typed offline
choices.why: That is the source of truth, and must never be evicted.

choices.text: notes the person pinned
choices.why: A pin is kept until the person removes it.

prompt: A catalogue changes once a term. A team sets max-age=0 on it to be safe. What does the lesson's reasoning say they lost?

choices.text: The ETag, which max-age=0 disables
choices.why: The tag still works; every read now uses it.

choices.text: The cache, which max-age=0 deletes
choices.why: The copy is kept; it is never trusted without a check.

choices.text: Safety: with max-age=0 the planner shows a stale catalogue for longer
choices.why: It does the reverse.

choices.text: Requests saved on most reads, and a screen that opens offline
choices.why: Right. How long to trust a copy is a question about the data, and this data changes rarely.

prompt: Why does lru.ts delete a cover's file before its row?

choices.text: SQLite refuses to delete a row whose file exists
choices.why: SQLite knows nothing about the file.

choices.text: Deleting files is faster
choices.why: Order, not speed, is the point.

choices.text: It leaves an orphan, never a false hit
choices.why: Right. A stop between the two leaves a file no row names, which the sweep of lesson 18 finds; no read mistakes it for a hit.

choices.text: The row holds the file's contents, so it has to be read first
choices.why: It holds the name, size and last use.
